# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [today's date]

**To:** Harvard Pilgrim Health Care, Member Appeals
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]
Member Services: 1-888-333-4742

**From:** Cameron Jennings
Member ID: W156639675
[My street address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-18 — Reference number POC-79A305E63C-48045 — ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888**

**Governing policy I am relying on:** Evolent Knee Arthroscopy Prior Authorization Tip Sheet (Evolent_CG-316), available at https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2024-02/2023%20Knee%20Arthroscopy%20Clin%20Tip%20Sheet%20Evolent%2002282024.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for the ACL reconstruction (CPT 29888) requested for me by my surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery. The notice dated 2026-08-18 states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision, because the plan's own published criteria ask for findings that my records already contain.

My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed. I am not a clinician, so below I have simply lined up the plan's own criteria next to what my records say.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. Imaging confirmation of the tear.** The policy states:

> "MRI results confirm complete ACL tear;"

My MRI of the knee, performed on 2026-06-11, shows a complete mid-substance tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with a bone bruise pattern. The menisci were intact and there was no significant arthritis. This is the exact finding the criterion describes, and it is the point on which my request was denied.

**2. Documentation of the imaging itself.** The policy states:

> "For all knee arthroscopy requests, the weight-bearing status of all X-rays should be documented in the office notes. If an MRI was performed, the actual MRI report should be included in the office notes as well."

The MRI report of 2026-06-11 is part of my file, and I am asking that it be re-read on this appeal. If the weight-bearing status of any X-rays is what the plan found missing, my surgeon's office can supply that documentation: [weight-bearing status of X-rays, to be confirmed by Dr. Marchetti's office]. If that is the gap, I ask the plan to say so directly so it can be corrected quickly rather than serving as a basis for denial.

**3. Instability.** The policy states:

> "Knee instability (as defined subjectively as "giving way", "giving out", "buckling", two-fist sign) with clinical findings of instability: Lachman's 1A, 1B, 2A, 2B, 3A, 3B, Anterior Drawer, Pivot Shift test, or instrumented (KT-1000 or KT-2000) laxity of greater than 3 mm side-side difference;"

My records document recurrent instability with pivoting, and that my knee has given way twice on stairs. My examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain. The specific test names and grades my surgeon recorded are in his chart: [specific instability test results as recorded by Dr. Marchetti].

**4. Absence of severe arthritis.** The policy states:

> "Member has no evidence of severe arthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence** Grade 3 or 4 [see grading appendix]) on weight-bearing x-rays; OR"

and elsewhere:

> "Member has no evidence of severe arthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4) on weightbearing x-rays"

My MRI of 2026-06-11 reports no significant arthritis. I am not able to tell from my paperwork whether a Kellgren-Lawrence grade was assigned on weight-bearing X-rays, and I do not want to claim a finding my records do not state. My surgeon's office can confirm that detail on request: [Kellgren-Lawrence grade on weight-bearing X-rays, if assigned].

**5. The supporting office documentation.** The policy states:

> "Office notes for arthroscopic knee surgery requests should document: o Symptom onset, duration, and severity; o Loss of function and/or limitations; o Type and duration of non-operative management modalities (where applicable)."

My records address each of these:

- **Onset, duration, severity:** 12 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest.
- **Loss of function:** recurrent instability with pivoting; the knee has given way twice on stairs; range of motion limited by pain.
- **Non-operative management and its duration:** supervised physical therapy for range of motion and quadriceps strengthening, with bracing, for 12 weeks from 2026-04-19 to 2026-07-12, 20 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note; NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief; and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-09 that gave 3 weeks of partial relief.

My records also note no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

**6. Surgical plan.** The policy states:

> "**Office notes should clearly state the surgical plan**"

The plan requested by my surgeon is ACL reconstruction, billed under CPT 29888. The full operative plan as written in my chart is: [surgical plan as stated in Dr. Marchetti's office note].

## Two points I am asking the plan to clarify

First, the policy contains the line:

> "At least ONE of the following criteria are met:"

That sentence introduces a list of further conditions that I have not been given a copy of. One of the alternatives I do have reads:

> "Acute ACL tear confirmed by MRI in high demand occupation or competitive athlete (any level of participation);"

and another reads:

> "MRI results confirm ACL tear associated with other ligamentous instability or repairable meniscus;"

I want to be accurate rather than sweeping: my MRI reports that my menisci are intact, so I am not asserting the meniscus pathway. On occupation and athletic participation, my records as I have them do not address that point, so I am not asserting it either; if it is relevant, my information is [my occupation and any athletic participation]. Because I cannot see the complete list of alternatives, **I am asking the plan to identify in writing which specific criteria it applied to my request and which one it found unmet.** Without that, I cannot know what evidence is thought to be missing, and neither can my surgeon.

Second, the denial says the imaging findings do not support medical necessity, but it does not say what the imaging was measured against. My MRI states a complete ACL tear, and the policy language quoted above asks for exactly that. I would appreciate an explanation of how that report was read to fall short.

## What I am asking for

Please overturn the denial dated 2026-08-18 (reference POC-79A305E63C-48045) and authorize the ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888, as requested by Dr. Marchetti. If any single document would resolve this, please tell me and my surgeon's office which one, and we will send it promptly. I also ask that this appeal be reviewed by a clinician with orthopedic expertise, and that I receive a written decision with the specific criteria relied upon.

I understand from my denial notice that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, meaning **by 2027-02-14**. I am submitting this letter to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, and I can be reached through Member Services at 1-888-333-4742 if anything further is needed from me.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at my file.

Sincerely,

**Cameron Jennings**
Member ID: W156639675
[Signature]
[Date signed]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

**Enclosures (to be attached):**
- Denial notice dated 2026-08-18, reference POC-79A305E63C-48045
- MRI report of the knee, 2026-06-11
- Office notes from Dr. Marchetti, MD, including surgical plan
- Physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-04-19 to 2026-07-12 (20 visits)
- [X-ray reports with weight-bearing status, if available]
- [Any additional records my surgeon's office wishes to include]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
